reference: Buoyancy-driven opening flow, neutral pressure level and the steady single-zone sensible heat balance implemented from CIBSE AM10 and ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals chapters 16 and 18, solved with scipy.optimize.brentq; cross-checked against the analytic two-opening stack formula.
reference_citations: CIBSE Applications Manual AM10, "Natural ventilation in non-domestic buildings", 2005, section 5 (stack-driven flow, neutral pressure level, discharge coefficient)

ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021), chapter 16 "Ventilation and Infiltration", thermal (stack) pressure difference dp = g (rho_o - rho_i) (z_NPL - z) and the orifice relation Q = Cd A sqrt(2 dp / rho)
ASHRAE Handbook - Fundamentals (2021), chapter 18 "Nonresidential Cooling and Heating Load Calculations", sol-air temperature Te = To + alpha It/ho - eps dR/ho
W.G. Brown and K.R. Solvason, "Natural convection through rectangular openings in partitions", Int. J. Heat Mass Transfer 5:859-868, 1962 (orifice/discharge coefficient convention)
tolerance: The stack relations, the neutral pressure level and the steady heat balance are closed forms, so the reference is exact to machine precision (scipy.optimize.brentq, xtol 1e-12). The tool stops its outer temperature loop when the indoor temperature moves less than 0.01 K, and that declared stopping criterion is what sets the tolerance: every quantity is graded with the change a 0.01 K shift of the indoor temperature produces in it (typically 2e-4 relative on the temperature and 6e-4 on the flows), floored at 2e-9. Bookkeeping identities - the five balance rows summing to zero, mass in + supply = mass out, ACH x volume = exhaust, the profile mean equalling the mean temperature, the gradient times the height equalling the top-to-bottom span - are exact arithmetic and are held to 1e-9 relative. The opening table is checked against velocity x area at the resolution the table itself prints (two decimals on the velocity).
not_benchmarked: Wind-driven ventilation: the tool does not model it at all. Its absence is checked, its magnitude is not.
The discharge coefficient Cd = 0.65 is a fixed convention, not a computed quantity; the harness checks that it is applied consistently, not that 0.65 is right for a given opening.

The stratification span S is an uncited heuristic. The harness checks the profile it produces is internally consistent (linear, mean equal to the zone temperature) and records the energy inconsistency it implies, but does not grade the value of S.

The clear-sky irradiance fit I = 1050 sin(beta)^1.15 and the cloud factor are a simple correlation with no published scatter statement; only its faithful implementation and its use in the sol-air temperature are checked.
The design outdoor temperatures in the built-in city list are data, not physics, and are not verified against a weather standard.
Transient behaviour, thermal mass, contaminant transport and local comfort are outside the model entirely.
run_notes: Driven through the DOM and the tool's own permalink codec; values read back from Diagram.record.build() and from the rendered opening table.

Cross-check: the network solver in the reference reproduces the analytic two-opening stack formula to better than 1e-10 relative on both the neutral plane and the mass flow, over four independent geometries.

The Boussinesq form Q = Cd A* sqrt(2 g dH dT/T_mean) quoted in CIBSE AM10 differs from the exact expression by a few per cent because it drops the density ratio; that gap is recorded as a property of the approximation, not of the tool.
crosscheck: exact two-opening closed form vs. the general network solver: < 1e-10 relative over four geometries; Boussinesq small-density-difference form: 1-6 % as expected.

cases.note: The tool solves buoyancy-driven ventilation only. ASHRAE Fundamentals ch. 16 combines stack and wind pressure as dp = dp_stack + dp_wind with dp_wind = Cp*rho*U^2/2; none of that is present here, so the absence must be stated in the limitations and in the model ranges, and the interface must not offer a wind input that does nothing.
no heat source, no sun, no supply: the driving force vanishes and the model must return zero flow and a finite temperature rather than NaN
every opening at the same height: the neutral plane degenerates and no stack flow is possible; the tool must not report a flow it cannot drive
a 0.01 m2 opening must be used as entered - not silently raised to a floor - and the printed area, the velocity and the flow must agree

flow_scales_with_area.note: two 0.01 m2 openings 7 m apart at ~50 K rise carry a few tens of m3/h, not thousands

cases.note: The encoded state must restore identical inputs and bit-identical outputs.
The ?lang= query parameter must select the tool UI language for all six catalogue languages.
The page loads only the two shared framework scripts from its own origin and fetches nothing, so network_access must be "none".

provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/gen_ventilation.py from the sources this artifact cites; that generator was re-run against this tree on 2026-10-03 and its output compared with the deployed corpus leaf by leaf at 1 893 leaves, 0 differing, so no case reuses a stored ref and none carries ref_source "recorded".
